posts.name: raga
posts.cooked: I received 38 marks after solving one question and potentially passing some additional test cases for others, but the passing criteria of 35 marks was not disclosed prior to the exam. I approached the exam with a strategy to gauge my preparation, deliberately avoiding exceeding 40 marks, even though I knew I could answer some questions correctly. My goal was to perform better in the re-exam because I recognized that my preparation wasn’t sufficient, particularly since I faced a full week of exams as a dual degree student. I was genuinely looking forward to this opportunity to improve, but the sudden announcement of the 35 marks passing criteria significantly disadvantages students like me who are committed to enhancing their grades. It’s essential for the assessment criteria to be transparent and fair, allowing everyone an equal chance to succeed. It is a humble request to solve this problem and allow us to appear in the re-OPPE. @sayan

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
It is not possible to schedule re-oppe for people who have passed.

Re-OPPE is meant for people who genuinely are unable to pass and need another chance, not for people "

23f2005445:

with a strategy to gauge my preparation, deliberately avoiding exceeding 40 marks,

"

Please prepare well for end term.
